nodes.summary: For a finite extension $q$ of a finite joint law $p$, viewed as the law of a triple $(X, Y, S)$ whose $(X, Y)$ marginal is $p$, this is $I(X; S) = H(X) + H(S) - H(X, S)$, where $H(X)$ is the Shannon entropy in bits of the $X$ marginal of $p$, and $H(S)$ and $H(X, S)$ are the Shannon entropies in bits of the $S$ and $(X, S)$ marginals of $q$.
nodes.title: Mutual information between the input and the auxiliary

nodes.summary: For a finite extension $q$ of a finite joint law $p$, viewed as the law of a triple $(X, Y, S)$ with $S$ taking values in $\{0, \dots, n_S - 1\}$, the auxiliary law is the marginal law of $S$ under $q$.
nodes.title: Auxiliary marginal of an extension

nodes.summary: The constant $c_c^*$ is the limit superior in the extended reals, as the real number $t$ tends to $+\infty$, of $W(t) - t - \log_2 t$, where $W(t)$ is the worst-case optimum at $t$: the supremum of the conditional-prefix optimum over all finite joint laws whose mutual information in bits is exactly $t$.
nodes.title: Channel simulation constant

nodes.summary: If the output alphabet of a finite joint law $p$ of $(X, Y)$ has exactly one element, then for every finite extension of $p$ by an auxiliary variable $S$, the conditional entropy $H(Y \mid S)$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Conditional entropy vanishes for a one-letter output

nodes.summary: For a finite extension $q$ of a finite joint law $p$, viewed as the law of a triple $(X, Y, S)$ whose $(X, Y)$ marginal is $p$, this is $H(Y \mid S) = H(Y, S) - H(S)$, where $H(Y, S)$ and $H(S)$ are the Shannon entropies in bits of the $(Y, S)$ and $S$ marginals of $q$.
nodes.title: Conditional entropy of the output given the auxiliary

nodes.summary: If the output alphabet of a finite joint law $p$ has exactly one element, then the conditional-prefix optimum of $p$ equals $0$.
nodes.title: The conditional-prefix optimum vanishes for a one-letter output

nodes.summary: For every finite joint law $p$ of $(X, Y)$, the conditional-prefix optimum of $p$ is at most the worst-case optimum at $t = I(X; Y)$, the mutual information of $p$ in bits.
nodes.title: The worst-case optimum dominates each conditional-prefix optimum

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a finite joint law of $(X, Y)$ and let $q$ be a finite extension of $p$ by an auxiliary variable $S$ with $I(X; S) = 0$ and $H(Y \mid X, S) = 0$. Then the conditional-prefix optimum of $p$ is at most the conditional entropy $H(Y \mid S)$ of $q$.
nodes.title: Each admissible extension bounds the conditional-prefix optimum

nodes.summary: For a finite joint law $p$ of $(X, Y)$, this is the infimum in the extended reals of the conditional entropy $H(Y \mid S)$ in bits over all finite extensions of $p$ by an auxiliary variable $S$ such that $I(X; S) = 0$ and $H(Y \mid X, S) = 0$. The infimum of the empty set is $+\infty$.
nodes.title: Conditional-prefix optimum of a joint law

nodes.summary: A finite extension of a finite joint law $p$ on $\{0, \dots, n_X - 1\} \times \{0, \dots, n_Y - 1\}$ consists of a positive integer $n_S$ and a probability law on triples $(x, y, s)$ with $s \in \{0, \dots, n_S - 1\}$ whose marginal on the pairs $(x, y)$ is exactly $p$.
nodes.title: Finite extension of a joint law

nodes.summary: A finite joint law consists of positive integers $n_X$ and $n_Y$ and a probability distribution on $\{0, \dots, n_X - 1\} \times \{0, \dots, n_Y - 1\}$.
nodes.title: Finite joint law

nodes.summary: A real number $\alpha$ is a uniform outer constant when there is a real $\beta > 0$ such that for every finite joint law $p$ of $(X, Y)$ there is a finite extension of $p$ by an auxiliary variable $S$ with $I(X; S) = 0$ and $H(Y \mid X, S) = 0$ and
nodes.title: Uniform outer constant for channel simulation

nodes.summary: Let $q$ be a finite extension of a finite joint law $p$ of $(X, Y)$ by an auxiliary variable $S$. Then the marginal of $X$ under the joint law of $(X, S)$ in $q$ equals the law of $X$ under $p$.
nodes.title: Input marginal of the input-auxiliary law

nodes.summary: Let $q$ be a finite extension of a finite joint law of $(X, Y)$ by an auxiliary variable $S$. Then the marginal of $S$ under the joint law of $(X, S)$ in $q$ equals the law of $S$ in $q$.
nodes.title: Auxiliary marginal of the input-auxiliary law

nodes.summary: Let $q$ be a finite extension of a finite joint law of $(X, Y)$, that is, a law of $((X, Y), S)$ with an auxiliary variable $S$. Its input-auxiliary law is the joint law of $(X, S)$: the image of the law of $q$ under $((x, y), s) \mapsto (x, s)$.
nodes.title: Input-auxiliary law

nodes.summary: The input law of a finite joint law $p$ on $\{0, \dots, n_X - 1\} \times \{0, \dots, n_Y - 1\}$ is its first marginal: the law on $\{0, \dots, n_X - 1\}$ that is the image of $p$ under $(x, y) \mapsto x$.
nodes.title: Input law

nodes.summary: The mutual information of a finite joint law $p$ of $(X, Y)$ is $I(X; Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X, Y)$, where $H(X)$ and $H(Y)$ are the Shannon entropies in bits of the input and output laws of $p$, and $H(X, Y)$ is the Shannon entropy in bits of $p$.
nodes.title: Mutual information

nodes.summary: Let $q$ be a finite extension of a finite joint law $p$ of $(X, Y)$ by an auxiliary variable $S$. Then the marginal of $Y$ under the joint law of $(Y, S)$ in $q$ equals the law of $Y$ under $p$.
nodes.title: Output marginal of the output-auxiliary law

nodes.summary: Let $q$ be a finite extension of a finite joint law of $(X, Y)$ by an auxiliary variable $S$. Then the marginal of $S$ under the joint law of $(Y, S)$ in $q$ equals the law of $S$ in $q$.
nodes.title: Auxiliary marginal of the output-auxiliary law

nodes.summary: Let $q$ be a finite extension of a finite joint law of $(X, Y)$, that is, a law of $((X, Y), S)$ with an auxiliary variable $S$. Its output-auxiliary law is the joint law of $(Y, S)$: the image of the law of $q$ under $((x, y), s) \mapsto (y, s)$.
nodes.title: Output-auxiliary law

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a finite joint law of an input $X$ and an output $Y$ whose output alphabet has exactly one letter. Then for every finite extension of $p$ by an auxiliary $S$, the conditional entropy $H(Y \mid X, S)$ of the output given the input and the auxiliary is $0$.
nodes.title: Zero output entropy given input and auxiliary for a one-letter output

nodes.summary: For a finite extension of a finite joint law, with input $X$, output $Y$ and auxiliary $S$, the conditional entropy of $Y$ given $(X, S)$ is $H(Y \mid X, S) = H(X, Y, S) - H(X, S)$, where $H$ denotes Shannon entropy in bits, $H(X, Y, S)$ is the entropy of the law of the extension and $H(X, S)$ is the entropy of its $(X, S)$ marginal.
nodes.title: Conditional entropy of the output given the input and the auxiliary

nodes.summary: The output law of a finite joint law $p$ of an input $X$ and an output $Y$ is the law of $Y$: the marginal of $p$ on the output alphabet, obtained by pushing $p$ forward along the projection onto the second coordinate.
nodes.title: Output law

nodes.summary: For every finite joint law $p$, the mutual information $I(X; S)$ between the input $X$ and the auxiliary $S$ in the trivial extension of $p$, whose auxiliary alphabet has a single letter, is $0$.
nodes.title: The trivial extension has zero auxiliary information

nodes.summary: For every finite joint law $p$, the auxiliary law of the trivial extension of $p$ is the point mass at $0$, the only letter of its one-letter auxiliary alphabet $\{0\}$.
nodes.title: Auxiliary law of the trivial extension

nodes.summary: For every finite joint law $p$ of an input $X$ and an output $Y$, the conditional entropy $H(Y \mid S)$ of the output given the auxiliary $S$ in the trivial extension of $p$ equals the Shannon entropy $H(Y)$ of the output law of $p$.
nodes.title: Conditional entropy in the trivial extension

nodes.summary: The trivial extension of a finite joint law $p$ of an input $X$ and an output $Y$ has the one-letter auxiliary alphabet $\{0\}$ and, as its law, the law of $((X, Y), 0)$ for $(X, Y)$ distributed according to $p$; its $(X, Y)$ marginal is $p$.
nodes.title: Trivial extension

nodes.summary: Call a real number $\alpha$ a uniform outer constant when there is a real $\beta > 0$ such that every finite joint law $p$ of an input $X$ and an output $Y$ has a finite extension by an auxiliary $S$ with $I(X; S) = 0$, $H(Y \mid X, S) = 0$ and $H(Y \mid S) \le I(X; Y) + \log_2(I(X; Y) + \beta) + \alpha$, where entropies and mutual informations are in bits. This is the infimum of the set of uniform outer constants,…
nodes.title: Infimum of the uniform outer constants

nodes.summary: For a real number $t$, the worst-case optimum at $t$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals, of the conditional-prefix optimum of $p$ over all finite joint laws $p$ of an input $X$ and an output $Y$ whose mutual information $I(X; Y)$, in bits, equals $t$; it is $-\infty$ when no such law exists.
nodes.title: Worst-case conditional-prefix optimum
Information Theory

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
